sections.content: Savannah, Georgia has a lot more going for it than Spanish moss and cobblestone streets. For real estate investors, it offers something even more appealing: a growing population, a booming tourism economy, a major port, and home prices that still leave room for solid profit margins. Whether you are a local wholesaler, an out-of-state flipper, or a long-distance landlord, finding real estate deals in Savannah GA is very much worth your attention right now. If you are new to the game, it helps to start with a solid foundation. Check out our guide on [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) before diving into market specifics.
Savannah GA Real Estate Market Overview

Savannah sits at the crossroads of several powerful economic forces. The Port of Savannah is the fastest-growing container port in the United States, attracting logistics companies, warehousing operations, and thousands of jobs. Meanwhile, the Savannah College of Art and Design (SCAD) brings a steady wave of students, faculty, and creative-industry professionals into the city year-round. Tourism adds another economic layer, with millions of visitors annually fueling short-term rental demand in the historic district. All of this adds up to a real estate market with strong fundamentals and growing long-term upside.
Average Home Prices in Savannah

As of 2024, the median home price in Savannah proper sits around $290,000 to $320,000, depending on the neighborhood and property condition. That number has climbed steadily over the past five years, up roughly 40% since 2019. In the historic district, you will find prices closer to $450,000 to $700,000 or higher for fully renovated properties. Meanwhile, transitional neighborhoods on the west and southside still offer homes in the $120,000 to $200,000 range, which is exactly where many investors find their best margins. Chatham County as a whole averages slightly lower, giving investors who look beyond city limits even more entry-level opportunities.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Savannah

Not every zip code in Savannah offers the same opportunity. Smart investors zero in on specific neighborhoods based on their strategy, whether that is wholesale, fix-and-flip, or buy-and-hold rentals. Here is a breakdown of the areas generating the most investor activity right now. You can also explore current deal flow directly on our [Savannah GA market page](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/savannah-ga).

items: Midtown Savannah (31405): A transitional area with older bungalows and ranch-style homes. Median prices around $180,000 to $240,000 make this a strong flip and wholesale target zone.
Thomas Square / Victorian District: High demand from SCAD students and young professionals. Renovated properties rent for $1,400 to $2,000 per month, making this ideal for BRRRR strategies.
Ardsley Park / Chatham Crescent: Established, higher-end neighborhood with stable values. Best for buy-and-hold investors seeking appreciation and lower vacancy rates.
West Savannah (31415): One of the most affordable entry points in the market. Distressed properties here can be acquired for $70,000 to $130,000 with flip ARVs of $190,000 to $240,000.
Pooler and Rincon (suburbs): Fast-growing bedroom communities near the port. New construction competes here, but older homes with deferred maintenance offer solid wholesale and rental plays.
Tybee Island: Premium short-term rental market. Vacation rental properties can generate $40,000 to $80,000 annually, though entry prices are higher at $450,000 and above.

sections.content: Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Savannah
Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling is active in Savannah, particularly in west side neighborhoods and transitional zip codes. The typical wholesale deal involves finding a distressed property, getting it under contract at a deep discount, and assigning that contract to a cash buyer for an assignment fee of $5,000 to $20,000. Motivated sellers in Savannah often include probate estates, absentee landlords with aging properties, and homeowners facing tax liens. To learn how to build a consistent pipeline of these deals, read our guide on [how to find off-market real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals). If you are just getting started with this strategy, our [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide walks you through every step of the process.
Fix-and-Flip Opportunities

Savannah's older housing stock, much of it built before 1980, means there is no shortage of properties needing renovation. A successful flip in midtown or the Victorian district might look like this: purchase at $155,000, invest $55,000 in renovations, and sell at an ARV of $265,000. That leaves a gross profit of roughly $55,000 before holding costs and closing fees. Use our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to run your own numbers before committing to any deal. The key in Savannah flips is accounting for older systems: knob-and-tube wiring, cast iron pipes, and pier-and-beam foundations are common in historic properties and can add significant rehab costs if not scoped properly.
Rental Properties and BRRRR Strategy

Long-term rentals in Savannah benefit from a large renter base driven by port workers, military families from nearby Fort Stewart, SCAD students, and healthcare workers. Average rents range from $1,100 for a basic two-bedroom up to $2,200 for a fully renovated three-bedroom in a desirable neighborhood. The BRRRR strategy (Buy, Rehab, Rent, Refinance, Repeat) works particularly well in Thomas Square and midtown, where you can buy distressed, renovate to current standards, pull out most of your equity via a cash-out refinance, and repeat the process with the same capital.

Before making an offer on any Savannah property, run it through a deal analyzer to verify your numbers hold up. Use our free [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to quickly calculate your maximum allowable offer, estimated profit, and assignment fee — all in under two minutes.
Savannah Real Estate Market Trends to Watch in 2024

items: Port expansion driving sustained job growth: Savannah's port handled a record volume of containers in 2023, and continued expansion is pulling in Amazon, Target, and other distribution giants, all of which need workforce housing.

Short-term rental regulation: The City of Savannah has tightened STR rules in the historic district. Investors should verify current licensing requirements before purchasing with an Airbnb strategy in mind.
Rising insurance costs: Like much of coastal Georgia, Savannah investors are seeing homeowner and landlord insurance premiums climb 15% to 25% annually. Factor this into your cash flow projections.

Interest rate sensitivity: Higher mortgage rates have slowed retail buyer demand, which actually creates more opportunity for cash buyers and wholesalers to negotiate favorable terms with motivated sellers.

New construction pressure in the suburbs: Pooler and Effingham County are seeing aggressive new construction that competes with rental properties. Stick to in-fill neighborhoods closer to the city core for stronger long-term demand.

sections.content: The best real estate markets are not the ones everyone is already talking about — they are the ones with real economic engines running underneath, where the fundamentals justify the price growth. Savannah has the port, the tourism, the university, and the military. That is a four-pillar market most cities would envy.
Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Savannah

Out-of-state investors are increasingly active in Savannah, attracted by the market's strong fundamentals and relative affordability compared to coastal markets in Florida or South Carolina. But investing remotely comes with its own set of challenges. Here is how to do it right.

items: Build your team before you buy: You need a local real estate attorney familiar with Georgia contract law, a reliable property inspector who knows older Savannah construction, a property manager with strong local references, and at least two or three licensed general contractors who can provide honest rehab estimates.

Use technology to find deals early: Platforms like AIWholesail aggregate off-market leads, distressed property data, and motivated seller signals so you can identify deals in Savannah before they hit the MLS. Getting in early is everything in a competitive market.

Understand Georgia-specific landlord laws: Georgia is considered a landlord-friendly state with relatively straightforward eviction processes, typically 30 to 45 days for non-payment. Still, work with a local attorney to ensure your leases are compliant.

Visit before you close, if at all possible: A single trip to walk properties, meet your contractor, and get a feel for neighborhoods will save you from costly mistakes. Drive west Savannah at different times of day before assuming an area is ready to invest.

Account for coastal risk: Savannah is in a zone with hurricane exposure. Flood zone designations can significantly impact insurance costs and financing. Always check FEMA flood maps and get insurance quotes before making offers.

Network with local wholesalers: Join the Savannah Real Estate Investors Association (REIA) or connect with local Facebook groups. Many of the best deals in Savannah never get listed publicly and go directly to buyers who have relationships with local wholesalers.

sections.content: Knowing how to spot a good deal is just as important as knowing where to look. If you want to sharpen your analysis skills, our guide on [how to analyze real estate deals like a pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) covers everything from running comps to stress-testing your cash flow assumptions in any market, including Savannah.

When evaluating Savannah rentals, target a minimum 1% rent-to-price ratio as a starting filter. A $180,000 property should ideally rent for at least $1,800 per month. In practice, you may find 0.8% in stronger neighborhoods, but anything below that deserves extra scrutiny on your cash flow projections before you commit.
Is Savannah the Right Market for You?

Savannah is not a get-rich-quick market, but it is a get-rich-steadily one. The economic fundamentals are real, the population is growing, and there are enough distressed properties and motivated sellers to keep active investors busy across multiple strategies. Whether you are looking to wholesale your first deal, flip a Victorian bungalow, or build a portfolio of cash-flowing rentals, real estate deals in Savannah GA offer compelling opportunities in 2024 and beyond. The investors who win here will be the ones who do their homework, build strong local teams, and move quickly when the right deal appears.
